tool_input.description: Run the arch check against deliberate violations

result:
The newsletter sign-up is in place as a self-contained module. `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` pass (16 tests, 13 of them new), and `bunx guren check` and `bunx guren check --arch` both report 0 failures; the 4 warnings from `guren check` are the missing-test warnings the baseline already had.

I confirmed the boundary rule works by temporarily adding a file under `app/` importing `modules/newsletter/index.ts` and one under `routes/` importing `modules/newsletter/db/schema.ts`. `guren check --arch` reported each as a failure and exited 1; I then removed both files.

Behaviours you might not assume:

- **Redirect after subscribe/unsubscribe:** the `Referer` is followed only when its host matches the request's host; otherwise the visitor goes to `/`. This prevents a crafted form from bouncing visitors to another site.
- **Emails are lowercased** before storing and looking up, so `Reader@Example.com` counts as already subscribed if `reader@example.com` exists.
- **Following a confirmation link twice** keeps the original confirmation time.
- **Root `db/schema.ts` has a one-line re-export** of the module's schema. This is how the framework's generator wires module tables so the usual migrate command sees them, and `guren check` verifies it; the table definition itself lives only in the module.
- **`bunx guren audit` now warns** that the two POST routes have no authentication check. That is intended, since guests must be able to subscribe.

**Summary of changes:** I scaffolded `modules/newsletter/` with the project's generators and filled it in: `index.ts` (module definition, `/newsletter` prefix), `routes.ts` (three named routes with validation schemas), `db/schema.ts` (the `newsletter_subscriptions` table), `app/Models/Subscription.ts` (64-hex-character random token, `token` hidden from serialization and not settable from requests), `app/Http/Validators/SubscriptionValidator.ts`, `app/Http/Controllers/SubscriptionController.ts`, and `tests/controllers/SubscriptionController.test.ts`. Outside the module, I added the migration `db/migrations/20260929161226_create_newsletter_subscriptions/`, a new `guren.arch.ts` that fails the checks if anything under `app/` or `routes/` imports from `modules/newsletter/` (type-only imports included), the module registration in `src/app.ts`, the schema re-export in `db/schema.ts`, `modules/**/*` in `tsconfig.json`'s include list, and the regenerated `.guren/routes.gen.ts` and `.guren/api-client.gen.ts`. Nothing under `app/` or `routes/` was touched.
